ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence screening of every UBO, director, officer and authorised signatory against: (i) the UK Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation Consolidated List and UK Sanctions List; (ii) the UN Security Council Consolidated List; (iii) the OFAC SDN List (secondary reference for financial institutions); (iv) the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; and (v) domestic Gibraltar and Cayman Islands sanctions regulations. PEP status is determined under the Gibraltar AML/CFT Code 2020 and FATF Recommendation 12, including family members and known close associates. Screening evidence, risk ratings and decision rationales must be retained for at least five years under the Proceeds of Crime Act 2015 (Gibraltar) and the Money Laundering Regulations (2023 Revision) (Cayman Islands).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Gibraltar Companies Registry operated under the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission ('Companies House Gibraltar'); name availability is verified by a GFSC-licensed corporate services provider through the Registrar's online name-search facility.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: English is the sole official and registry language. Names must be expressed in Roman (Latin) alphabetic characters A-Z and Arabic numerals 0-9, together with permitted punctuation. No transliteration into non-Latin scripts is accepted. A Cayman exempted company registering as a foreign company must use its exact Cayman-law name, including the mandatory suffix 'Limited' or 'Ltd.', without substantive translation. The Registrar refuses names that are identical or substantially similar to an existing Gibraltar registered name, misleading, offensive, or suggestive of a connection with the Crown, HM Government of Gibraltar, a municipal authority, or a public body.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name refusal, the applicant's licensed corporate services provider may file a written reconsideration request with the Registrar of Companies within 14 days of the refusal notice, stating the legal grounds and exhibiting an updated negative name-search certificate. The Registrar must issue a reasoned decision within 14 days. If the refusal is upheld, the applicant may file an originating application to the Supreme Court of Gibraltar under the Companies Act 2014 seeking a declaration that the name is not prohibited, misleading, or offensive. A name reservation may be extended once for an additional 30 days upon payment of the prevailing extension tariff, provided no adverse search result or conflicting registration has intervened.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office with no physical operational footprint is not acceptable as the statutory registered office. The Gibraltar foreign company must maintain a physical registered office in Gibraltar where service of process can be effected and statutory records kept, normally at the premises of a GFSC-licensed corporate services provider. The underlying Cayman exempted company must similarly maintain a physical registered office in the Cayman Islands with a licensed registered office provider. A virtual-office arrangement for administrative correspondence and remote AIGC SaaS operations is permissible only as an ancillary measure and cannot replace the physical statutory registered office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low quantified risk: approximately 5% annual probability of an unannounced physical inspection by the Registrar of Companies or the Gibraltar Financial Intelligence Unit for a standard, non-licensed, low-risk AIGC SaaS foreign company. The likelihood rises materially to approximately 20-30% if the company later becomes a licensed financial services or DLT provider, or if adverse intelligence or AML/CFT typology alerts are triggered.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Cayman Islands Companies Act (2024 Revision), Part VI (Exempted Companies) and continuation provisions; Gibraltar Companies Act 2014, Sections 386-394 (continuation of foreign companies into Gibraltar); Gibraltar Income Tax (Companies) regime governing exempt non-resident status
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cayman Islands Registrar of Companies (General Registry) for originating incorporation; Gibraltar Companies House, Registrar of Companies, for continuation-in and statutory registration
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum and Articles of Association of an Exempted Company together with Gibraltar Certificate of Continuation
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under Cayman or Gibraltar law; the company may be incorporated with a single USD 1.00 paid-up ordinary share. A subscribed but unpaid share capital balance may be held in escrow with the licensed Gibraltar corporate services provider pending funding of a Gibraltar EMI bank account, solely to satisfy bank due-diligence capital-evidence requirements.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, as first board resolutions: (1) the Memorandum and Articles of Association, as filed with the Gibraltar Registrar, be adopted and ratified; (2) the registered office be situated with the licensed corporate services provider in Gibraltar, which is appointed registered agent; (3) the subscribers be allotted fully paid ordinary shares as recorded in the register of members; (4) the directors and officers named in the register of directors be appointed, and the company secretary and compliance officer be authorised to file statutory returns, open bank accounts, execute AI video generation SaaS agreements, and take all acts necessary to commence operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserved Company Name Search and AML/KYC Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Companies House electronic name-search portal via licensed corporate services provider (CSP)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Run a Gibraltar company-name availability search and reserve the intended AI SaaS trading name; concurrently submit the statutory customer due-diligence pack covering ultimate beneficial owners, directors, source of funds and source of wealth for clearance under Gibraltar AML/CFT obligations.
required_dossiers: Completed name availability search report
Name reservation request form
Certified true copy of passport of each director and UBO
Proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement, under 3 months old)
Banking reference letter confirming source of funds
Declaration of Ultimate Beneficial Owner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused as undesirably confusing, submit up to three alternative names in rank order for re-search; if AML clearance is queried, provide a notarized statement of wealth and an independent legal reference letter within 5 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Incorporation of the Cayman Exempted Company
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cayman Islands Registrar of Companies (General Registry) lodged through a licensed Cayman registered-office provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Lodge the notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association in the exempted-company statutory form, together with Form 1 (notice of registered office), Form 2 (notice of directors and secretary), and the registered-office provider's consent; pay the prescribed fee and obtain the Certificate of Incorporation of an Exempted Company.
required_dossiers: Memorandum and Articles of Association (exempted company form)
Form 1 — Notice of Registered Office
Form 2 — Notice of Directors, Secretary and Registered Office
Consent of registered office provider
Notarized proof of identity of incorporator and subscribers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Cayman Registrar issues a requisition for defective documents, file amended M&A or Forms within 10 business days; if filing is rejected, re-file with corrections and apply for expedited registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Continuation of the Exempted Company into Gibraltar and Re-registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Companies House — Registrar of Companies (continuation-in under the Gibraltar Companies Act 2014)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the Cayman Registrar's certificate authorizing continuation out and a certificate of good standing; submit to the Gibraltar Registrar the continuation application with constitutional documents and a declaration of solvency; upon approval, collect the Gibraltar Certificate of Continuation and the Gibraltar company registration number.
required_dossiers: Cayman special resolution approving continuation out
Cayman Certificate of Good Standing
Cayman Registrar consent to continuation
Declaration of solvency signed by all directors
Gibraltar continuation application form
Constitutional documents certified by the Cayman Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Gibraltar Registrar queries documentation, submit a supplementary legal opinion confirming compliance with continuation procedure; if Cayman consent is refused, appeal on procedural grounds or, alternatively, form a new Gibraltar company with substantially identical constitutional terms.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting, Registered Office Adoption, and Officer Appointments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors convened at the Gibraltar registered office of the licensed CSP
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the statutory first board meeting; adopt the pro-forma first board resolution approving the constitutional documents, adoption of the Gibraltar registered office, and appointment of directors, company secretary and compliance officer; execute the registers of members and directors, and issue share certificates to subscribers.
required_dossiers: Pro-forma first board resolution (minutes)
Register of members (share allotment)
Register of directors and company secretary
Consent to act forms executed by each officer
Registered office consent letter of the Gibraltar CSP
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the board cannot convene physically, adopt written resolutions under the company's articles; if an appointee declines, appoint an alternate by board resolution and file the updated officer notice with the Registrar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Formation Statutory Returns, Beneficial Ownership Registration, and Nil-Licensing Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Companies House (returns desk) and the Commissioner of Income Tax, Gibraltar
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the incorporation confirmation return and register persons with significant control in Gibraltar's Beneficial Ownership Register (BOO); obtain the Gibraltar tax reference number and file the non-resident/exempt status declaration; record a statutory file note confirming that ISIC 6201/NAICS 511210 AI software activities trigger no industrial, environmental, fire-safety or occupational licensing requirement absent a physical premises; adopt a standing instruction to procure clearances if premises are later occupied.
required_dossiers: Incorporation confirmation return
BOO Register PSC filings
Tax registration form and corporate tax ID confirmation
Directors' declaration on exempt non-resident status
Legal opinion confirming nil industrial and environmental licensing exposure
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the BOO filing is returned for incomplete UBO identification, correct and resubmit within 5 working days; if the tax office queries exempt status, supply the Gibraltar Certificate of Continuation and the directors' declaration of non-residence.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — ISIC 6201 (computer programming) and NAICS 511210 (software publishing) are non-industrial activities; Gibraltar Ministry of Digital and Financial Services is the policy authority but issues no operational license for pure software
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — no operating or manufacturing permit triggers for AIGC video-generation SaaS delivered via Stripe and Paddle payment rails

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of the Environment, Heritage and Climate Change, HM Government of Gibraltar
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — digital software business with no physical development and no emissions source; no EIA screening or registration required at formation
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable — zero industrial discharge. Cloud-hosted AI video synthesis generates no on-site wastewater, VOC or particulate emissions; if a workspace is later established, apply Gibraltar/EU ambient noise and electronic-waste (WEEE) compliance thresholds.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not required at formation for an unbundled remote AI software company; upon lease of any physical premises, the Company must obtain Gibraltar Fire and Rescue Service fire-safety certification, a structural load certificate for occupancy, and an occupational health-and-safety workplace clearance under Gibraltar Health and Safety at Work legislation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: HM Government of Gibraltar — Income Tax Office (Commissioner of Income Tax); official e-services and guidance portal: https://www.gibraltar.gov.gi/taxation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Cayman Exempted Company is treated as an overseas company for Gibraltar registration purposes. The foreign entity must first register with the Registrar of Companies under the Gibraltar Companies Act 2014 as an overseas company (appointing a Gibraltar registered office and a local authorised agent), then file the Income Tax application for a Gibraltar Tax Reference Number (TRN) with the Income Tax Office. The file must include the Cayman Certificate of Incorporation, the Certificate of Good Standing issued by the Cayman Registrar of Companies, constitutional documents, director/shareholder register, declaration of central management and control, and AML/KYC identification of beneficial owners; the TRN is issued upon a satisfactory substance and residence assessment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone: as a Cayman Exempted Company the entity holds Cayman exempt status free of income tax; in Gibraltar classification is separate and residence-based. If the board of directors passes resolutions and exercises senior management control in Gibraltar, the company will be classified Entity_Level_Taxation — resident and taxable at the 12.5% Gibraltar corporate rate on trading profits with worldwide territorial scope consistent with OECD practice; otherwise, if control remains in Cayman and only a sales presence exists in Gibraltar, the company is non-resident but remains exposed to Gibraltar corporation tax on Gibraltar-source income attributable to a permanent establishment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Gibraltar does not offer a check-the-box pass-through regime. Available statutory elections: (1) Qualifying Company (QC) election — available to a non-resident company with exclusively foreign-source income, introducing a deemed gross-margin charge rather than an ordinary accounting profit basis, subject to OECD Substance Requirement compliance; (2) group relief election to surrender losses within a Gibraltar tax-consortium group; (3) administrative advance ruling pathway whereby the Commissioner may certify non-residence based on board-meeting minutes, staff locations, and closed management records held outside Gibraltar.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT/GST is not levied in Gibraltar. The applicable indirect tax architecture is Import Duty and Excise Duty under the Customs and Excise Duties Act, Business Property Duty (on occupational premises), and Insurance Premium Duty. Cross-border digital services (AI video-generation SaaS performed abroad) fall outside all Gibraltar indirect tax heads of charge.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No Gibraltar VAT registration is possible because no VAT regime exists; no local economic-turnover threshold is therefore applicable. Import Duty applies to physical goods entering Gibraltar irrespective of monetary threshold. The Cayman entity's digital SaaS export has zero indirect tax liability in Gibraltar. Separate UK VAT registration may be triggered where UK B2C digital supplies exceed the GBP 85,000 threshold (HMRC Making Tax Digital e-return obligations then apply).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Gibraltar imposes no real-time fiscal clearance, API clearance, digital stamping, or B2B/B2C e-invoicing network mandate. Issuance of commercial invoices in electronic form is unrestricted; invoices must satisfy the Income Tax Act content requirements (date, unique number, supplier/recipient identification, TRN, currency). Retention in an accessible e-archive for six years is required, with periodic Income Tax risk-based assessment audits able to require invoice-level data extracts via Gibraltar Regulatory Authority data-sharing powers.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating per se is not available as Gibraltar has no VAT. Instead, the AI avatar video-generation SaaS qualifies for a complete statutory exclusion from Gibraltar Import Duty as an offshore services supply. The claim requires demonstrable export substance: contracts concluded outside Gibraltar or via a non-Gibraltar payment processor, software hosted on non-Gibraltar cloud infrastructure, and no handover or performance occurring in Gibraltar customs territory.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Gibraltar Customs Export Declaration for movement of any physical servers/hardware plus a service-export statement for digital SaaS deliverables
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill for physical exports, or cloud hosting / CDN access logs, signed AI-SaaS subscription agreements and Stripe/Paddle payout records for digital supplies
Inward Remittance Certificate from a Gibraltar-licensed bank identifying the counterparty, invoice reference, and currency settlement
Intercompany services agreement and master file evidencing OECD-aligned transfer pricing between the Cayman entity and any UK/EU affiliates
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export-relief claims and offshore routing are reviewed by the Income Tax Office under the UK-Gibraltar Exchange of Information Agreements. A failed substantiation results in an upward assessment of the full AI SaaS turnover at 12.5% Gibraltar tax plus (i) penalty for careless inaccuracy of up to 30% of underpaid tax, (ii) fraud penalty of up to 100% of underpaid tax, (iii) statutory late-payment interest from the original due date, and (iv) unfettered six-year reopening of assessments, extended indefinitely if fraud is proven. Directors risk disqualification orders under the Companies Act 2014 for false documentary certification.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Cayman Islands Monetary Authority (CIMA) — the monetary authority, currency board, and financial services regulator of the Cayman Islands, responsible for issuing and backing the Cayman Islands dollar (KYD); for the Gibraltar treasury leg, the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC) under the Financial Services (Banking) Act, together with Her Majesty's Government of Gibraltar Treasury. Neither territory operates a conventional central bank with exchange-control powers; CIMA administers monetary stability but does not impose foreign-exchange controls.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Cayman Islands maintains fully unrestricted current-account and capital-account convertibility. The KYD is pegged to the United States dollar at the statutory rate of 1.00 KYD = 1.20 USD (equivalently, USD 1.00 = KYD 0.8333); US dollars circulate freely and are accepted in commerce. There are no restrictions on dividend distributions, profit remittances, royalty payments, intercompany loans, or liquidation proceeds payable to the Gibraltar parent or any foreign shareholder, and no CIMA permission or exchange-control consent is required. The Gibraltar leg is equally liberal: the Gibraltar pound (GIP) is pegged at par to sterling and capital moves freely between Gibraltar, the United Kingdom, and the rest of the world. For the United Kingdom sovereign overlay, the Exchange Control Act 1947 has been effectively repealed since 1979, so no Bank of England, FCA, or HMRC approval is required for UK investors funding the structure. The operative constraints are bank-level rather than regulatory: source-of-funds verification, Cayman economic-substance evidence under the International Tax Co-operation (Economic Substance) Act, and OFAC, EU, and UN sanctions screening at correspondent banks in New York or London.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Neither the Cayman Islands nor Gibraltar imposes any statutory timeline for repatriating export proceeds, any mandatory conversion ratio, or any surrender obligation in respect of foreign-currency receipts. A Cayman exempted company carrying on AI-avatar-video SaaS business may retain 100% of its Stripe and Paddle settlement proceeds, subscription revenue, and other export receipts in USD, EUR, GBP, or any freely convertible currency, and may hold such proceeds offshore indefinitely without CIMA notification. Correspondent banks in the United States and United Kingdom will, however, apply OFAC and financial-sanctions screening, and wire transfers must carry complete originator and beneficiary information in accordance with FATF Recommendation 16.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (USD multi-currency) and Capital Escrow Account for subscribed share capital
Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return and annual government fee (Companies Act, s.261 & Sixth Schedule)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, General Registry, Grand Cayman
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 January each year for the calendar year ended 31 December; first return due 31 January following incorporation (fee prorated to one half if incorporated on or after 1 July)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unpaid/unfiled by 31 January: Registrar issues 30-day default notice; thereafter penalty of 10% of the annual fee accrues per month of continued default; persistent default triggers strike-off and dissolution under s.263.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Economic Substance Notification (ESN) - annual declaration of relevant-activity status
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department for International Tax Cooperation (DITC), Cayman Islands
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 January following the end of each financial year (by 31 January for a 31 December FYE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fixed penalty of CI$10,000 (approx. US$12,195) for late or non-filed ESN; continued default may be reported by the Tax Information Authority to the Registrar and lead to strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Economic Substance (ES) Return - required only if the company carries on a relevant activity (e.g., IP holding or distribution/service-centre income)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department for International Tax Cooperation (DITC), Cayman Islands
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months after the end of the financial year (by 31 December of the following year for a 31 December FYE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Initial penalty CI$10,000 (approx. US$12,195); continued default attracts an additional CI$100,000 (approx. US$121,951) and/or up to 5 years' imprisonment for officers; strike-off may follow on referral from the Tax Information Authority.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return of an overseas company with a Gibraltar place of business (Companies Act 2014, overseas-company provisions)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 28 days after the anniversary of the company's registration in Gibraltar (the return date)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties escalate from GIP 150 to GIP 1,500 by length of default; daily default fines and criminal fines up to GIP 5,000 apply to officers; persistent default enables the Registrar to strike off the Gibraltar registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Gibraltar Economic Substance Report under the Income Tax (Economic Substance) Regulations - applicable only if the company is tax-resident in Gibraltar and carries on a relevant activity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commissioner of Income Tax, HM Government of Gibraltar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months after the end of the accounting period (aligned to the Gibraltar corporate tax return date)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing triggers escalating financial penalties and daily default fines; knowingly false statements are a criminal offence; the Commissioner may notify the Registrar, exposing the company to strike-off of its Gibraltar registration.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory audit for an unregulated Cayman Exempted Company under the Companies Act; audit applies only if the Articles so require, CIMA licensing applies (not applicable to ISIC 6201 SaaS), or shareholders holding at least 25% of votes demand an audit under s.59. In Gibraltar, a registered overseas company is exempt from audit and account-filing where it meets the small-company test (at least two of: turnover <= GIP 10.2M, balance-sheet total <= GIP 5.1M, average employees <= 50).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Cayman law prescribes no statutory GAAP; IFRS is the market standard for cross-border AIGC SaaS entities (US GAAP is acceptable for US-investor reporting). Gibraltar filings, where triggered, must follow IFRS as adopted by the EU/UK on a true-and-fair basis. Cayman Companies Act s.60 requires accounting records to be retained for at least 5 years; Gibraltar tax records must be kept 6 years; a 7-year retention policy is the professional standard for this structure.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No standalone annual UBO filing exists in either jurisdiction. Each year-end the Cayman registered agent circulates a beneficial-ownership confirmation; directors must certify the Beneficial Ownership Register (BOR) and any change in shareholding or control of the AI-avatar business must be filed with the Cayman BOSS portal within 14 days of the change, and with the Gibraltar central beneficial-ownership register within 14 days if a Gibraltar registration is maintained. The annual confirmation is evidenced by the agent's compliance certificate issued before the 31 January Cayman annual-return date.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of directors' and members' meetings
Register of Mortgages and Charges (if any)
Beneficial Ownership Register (maintained at the Cayman registered office and filed through the BOSS portal)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$1,200 - US$3,500 per annum for Cayman registered office, registered agent and corporate administrator; add US$500 - US$1,500 per annum if a Gibraltar registered address and local agent are maintained
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$8,000 - US$20,000 for a voluntary IFRS audit of a small Cayman Exempted Company with Gibraltar operations; US$3,000 - US$6,000 for a compilation or review-only engagement

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% Cayman corporate income tax on exempted company profits; if the company becomes tax-resident in Gibraltar by central management and control or carries on business through a Gibraltar permanent establishment, Gibraltar corporation tax applies at 12.5% on Gibraltar-source chargeable profits.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Cayman Statutory 30-year tax exemption undertaking under Section 6 of the Companies Act covering profits, income, gains, distributions, interest, royalties, and capital gains; no Gibraltar capital gains tax and no Gibraltar withholding taxes on dividends; if Gibraltar-taxable, only ordinary deductions and capital allowances are available, with no standalone patent box concession for AI avatar software unless qualifying local R&D expenditure is present.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Cayman Companies Act Annual Return of an Exempted Company, filed electronically through the Cayman Islands General Registry 'Company Annual Return' module.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due by 31 January following each calendar year; a newly registered exempted company must file its first annual return within 60 days of the anniversary of incorporation when the registration falls within that calendar year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name of the Cayman exempted company, registration number, and date of incorporation exactly as displayed on the Certificate of Incorporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the exact Cayman legal name; do not trade under the Gibraltar branch name in this box and do not substitute the AI video SaaS brand name.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box B — Registered Office and Registered Agent
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cayman Islands registered office address, registered agent name and licence number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign manager or Gibraltar office cannot be stated as the registered office; the Cayman registered agent must be named in full.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Authorised capital, issued shares, and class of shares including subscriber shares.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Nominal issued capital is sufficient; do not declare foreign branch capital, and state nil for any non-Cayman share premium unless already recorded.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full names, nationality, usual residential addresses of all directors and the company secretary.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident directors may be listed; the registered agent must retain passport copy, proof of address, and source-of-funds documents for the beneficial owner.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box E — Declarations and Fee Classification
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of exempted status, annual return fee classification, and confirmation that any Economic Substance Return or Beneficial Ownership Return obligations are current.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State that the company is not trading in the Cayman Islands or expressly indicate the relevant ESR activity if the AI avatar video operations create any Cayman relevant activity.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers the statutory annual fee surcharge and daily late fees imposed by the Cayman Companies Management Authority; continued non-filing permits the Registrar to strike the exempted company off the register and dissolve it, with directors personally exposed to restoration costs and penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Gibraltar Corporation Tax Return, Form CT-1, filed through the Gibraltar Department of Tax and Customs eTax portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within nine months after the end of the chargeable accounting period; for a company with a 31 December year-end, the return is due by 30 September the following year, unless the Commissioner grants an extension.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total trading profits arising in Gibraltar, foreign-source profits of a Gibraltar-resident company, and all profits attributable to a permanent establishment operating in Gibraltar.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Cayman exempted company with only a Gibraltar PE, enter only the profits attributable to the Gibraltar office and exclude worldwide SaaS revenue not connected to Gibraltar.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Expenditure wholly and exclusively incurred in producing gross chargeable profits, plus statutory capital allowances.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not deduct Cayman exempted-company formation fees unless demonstrably linked to Gibraltar revenue; transfer pricing adjustments for AI IP licences must be reflected here.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net chargeable profits after deductions, capital allowances, loss claims, and any transfer pricing adjustment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cayman tax exemption has no effect on Gibraltar Box 3 profits; the Gibraltar PE cannot be ignored merely because the parent is Cayman-exempt.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gibraltar corporation tax computed on adjusted chargeable profits before any double taxation relief.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not claim a credit for hypothethical Cayman tax; no Cayman income tax has actually been paid.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credit relief or deduction available under an applicable double taxation arrangement for foreign tax paid on the same profits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a documentary Tax Residence Certificate and specific DTA claim; the Cayman tax exemption undertaking is not a TRC and cannot be used to reduce Gibraltar tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 — Transfer Pricing and Economic Substance Declaration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of controlled transactions, intragroup IP royalty payments, and the location of staff, offices, and management for the AI avatar video generation business.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If a Gibraltar PE exists, complete the Gibraltar Economic Substance schedule and state the arm's-length methodology applied to SaaS licence fees; retain the Local File for inspection.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing incurs a fixed penalty plus daily default fines and a 10% surcharge on unpaid corporation tax after six months, with an additional 10% after twelve months; for fraudulent returns, civil penalties can reach 200% of the tax evaded and criminal prosecution may follow.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% statutory withholding tax on dividends paid by a Cayman exempted company; 0% Gibraltar statutory withholding on dividends paid to non-residents.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: A Cayman exempted company does not qualify for traditional double taxation treaty relief because it pays no Cayman tax. To obtain reduced withholding in a source state, the beneficial owner must actually be tax-resident elsewhere and must submit: (i) a formal treaty claim on the source state's prescribed form, (ii) an official Tax Residence Certificate from the revenue authority of the residence state, (iii) a declaration of beneficial ownership, and (iv) evidence that no permanent establishment in the source state is present. For profits taxable in Gibraltar, any claimed relief under arrangements with other jurisdictions is raised in Box 5 of Form CT-1 and strictly requires residence certificates and beneficial ownership statements before the reduction is granted.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Cayman: no domestic withholding tax on outbound royalties or interest (0%). Gibraltar: no domestic withholding tax on royalty or interest payments to non-residents (0%). A foreign AI IP licensor may nonetheless have Gibraltar corporation tax exposure at 12.5% if the royalties are effectively connected with a Gibraltar PE or if transfer pricing rules recharacterise the payments as Gibraltar-source profits.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Cayman ESR threshold: no monetary de minimis; every exempted company carrying on a relevant activity must file an annual Economic Substance Return. Gibraltar TP documentation threshold: GIP 1,000,000 of annual controlled turnover; a Local File is required where controlled transactions, including AI IP licence fees and video-generation API payments, exceed GIP 250,000; a Master File and country-by-country notification are required for groups with consolidated turnover above GIP 50,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Cayman Economic Substance Law 2019 and Gibraltar Economic Substance Act 2018 both apply to relevant activities including IP holding, distribution, financing, and service-centre operations. An AI avatar video generation business that licenses algorithms, processes content, or provides technical services to affiliates must demonstrate actual premises, full-time employees, regular board meetings with strategic management, and expenditure proportionate to income in the jurisdiction where substance is claimed. A Cayman exempted company that is tax-resident outside Cayman can file an exclusion statement; if managed from Gibraltar, it must additionally satisfy the Gibraltar economic substance test and cannot rely on the Cayman exemption letter as proof of substance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Gibraltar Corporation Tax Fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Funelling Gibraltar PE profits into a Cayman exempted company through artificially inflated AI licence fees; omitting the Gibraltar business from Form CT-1 Box 1; filing a false Cayman ESR exclusion; or causing retail SaaS revenues from Stripe or Paddle to be hidden within the Cayman entity while all management and contract execution occur in Gibraltar.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Gibraltar Income Tax Act and criminal law, an unlimited fine on indictment and imprisonment of up to seven years; civil penalties up to 200% of the underpaid tax, plus statutory interest and freezing of payment processor accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the ultimate beneficial owner can be made jointly and severally liable for the evaded tax; the court may pierce the Cayman corporate veil, issue travel bans, disqualify directors, and impose personal confiscation orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Economic Substance Violation / Shell Company Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the AI video synthesis IP in a Cayman exempted company with no office, no employees, no bank account activity, and no board meetings in Cayman, while claiming a zero-tax status and ignoring Gibraltar-source profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Cayman Economic Substance Law penalties: US$10,000 for an initial ESR violation, US$10,000 for each subsequent six-month period of default, with a maximum penalty of US$500,000; Gibraltar ESR Act penalties include substantial fines, default daily penalties, and cancellation of the Gibraltar permanent establishment registration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for ESR filings and can be disqualified for up to ten years in Gibraltar and five years in Cayman; personal asset restraint orders and director travel bans are available where the company is a pure shell used to shelter SaaS revenue.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the AI avatar video platform through a Cayman exempted company without filing a Beneficial Ownership Return, without a designated AML compliance officer, without KYC/CDD on Stripe or Paddle subscribers, and using bearer or digital shares to conceal the true owner of deepfake-software revenue.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Cayman Proceeds of Crime Act and AML Regulations, penalties include fines, imprisonment of up to two years on summary conviction and five years on indictment; Gibraltar Proceeds of Crime Act sanctions include up to seven years' imprisonment and unrestricted fines for laundering arrangements or false beneficial ownership declarations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The nominated officer and each director are personally liable for a false beneficial ownership register and for failure to file suspicious activity reports; travel bans, extradition to the United Kingdom or United States, and personal confiscation orders are available.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing / Profit Shifting Documentation Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Transferring AI avatar video-generation IP to the Cayman exempted company at nominal value, charging the Gibraltar branch super-royalities, booking all consumer SaaS revenue to Cayman, or failing to prepare Local File, Master File, and economic substance documentation for intragroup AI licensing transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Gibraltar tax authorities may adjust chargeable profits under OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines and impose penalties ranging from 10% of the adjustment to 100% of the understated tax in serious non-disclosure cases, plus daily default fines; Cayman ESR penalties up to US$500,000 also apply for an uncorrected false return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign the Gibraltar return without contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation are personally liable for negligent certification; false transfer pricing declarations trigger criminal fraud liability, director disqualification, and if the Cayman company is treated as a sham, joint and several liability to third-party creditors.
